description: We are a team of students with a shared interest in space exploration and science. For the NASA Space Apps, we came together to develop Earth2Space, an interactive platform that helps people discover Earth's extreme environments that could serve as analogs for permanent Moon base locations and Mars. We aim to make complex scientific information easier to understand and explore. As young learners, we hope future generations will be inspired to take part in future space exploration.
summary:
We developed Earth2Space, an interactive web platform for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It identifies and showcases 30 proposed extreme terrestrial locations around the world that may serve as analogs for permanent Moon base locations and Mars. The platform features an interactive map with real geographic coordinates, filterable location profiles, Moon and Mars comparisons, and a step-by-step guide to space mission preparation.
Earth2Space addresses the challenge by helping users discover Earth environments that share similar characteristics with potential lunar base sites and Martian landscapes, such as extreme temperatures, volcanic terrain and subsurface ice. Users can filter locations according to their relevance to the Moon, Mars or both, making it easier to understand their potential uses in space research.
This project is important because studying these Earth analogs allows researchers to investigate challenging environments and test technologies, such as rovers, spacesuits and habitats, before using them in space. This can help reduce mission risks and support the development of safer, more sustainable human settlements beyond Earth.
details:
🌏What if exploring Mars and the Moon could begin right here on Earth? That is the idea behind Earth2Space, an interactive educational website that takes users around the world to discover places with environments similar to those found on other planets. These places are known as Earth analogs — locations that share certain environmental or geological features with the Moon or Mars. Featuring 30 proposed research locations, Earth2Space demonstrates how studying Earth's extreme environments can help scientists understand the challenges of space exploration and prepare for future missions.

🚀 Features and How It Works

  • Interactive World Map: Users can search, zoom in and explore 30 research locations using map markers.
  • Location Profiles: Each location provides information about its environment, planetary connection and evidence status. Some locations provide images and 360° views to enhance visualisations.
  • Location Filters: Users can narrow down locations based on their environment and connection to the Moon or Mars.
  • Planet Comparison: A feature that helps users understand the similarities and differences between the Moon and Mars.
  • Educational Quiz: Allows users to test their knowledge of Earth analogs and space exploration.
  • Mission Preparation & Timeline: Explains how Earth analogs are used in research and shows the steps towards future space missions.
  • Adjust Your Preferences: Users can switch between light mode or dark mode and between languages English and Bahasa Melayu with a single button.
  • Interactive Simulations: Features hands-on experiences such as the Rover Challenge and other space exploration activities, allowing users to explore mission-related challenges, test their knowledge and better understand the difficulties of exploring the Moon and Mars.

🌱 Key Benefits & Impact

  • Makes space science more accessible and easier to understand.
  • Helps raise awareness of how Earth's environments contribute to space research.
  • Provides an educational platform where users can explore scientific information independently.
  • Inspires curiosity about science, technology and future space discoveries.

🤝 Who Benefits from Earth2Space?

  • Scientists & Researchers: Helps identify and study Earth locations that could serve as analogs for permanent Moon bases and Mars environments.
  • Space Agencies: Provides an accessible overview of potential research sites that could support mission planning and preparation.
  • Students & Educators: Makes learning about planetary environments and space exploration more engaging through interactive maps, comparisons and simulations.
  • Future Space Explorers: Helps build an understanding of the environmental challenges astronauts may face when living and working beyond Earth.
  • Space Enthusiasts: Allows people interested in astronomy and space exploration to discover Earth analog locations, explore interactive simulations and learn more about future Moon and Mars missions.
  • General Public: Raises awareness of how Earth's extreme environments can contribute to future space discoveries.

💻 Tools & Technologies

  • Lovable: Used to develop and design the website.
  • Interactive Digital Maps: Used to display and navigate the different research locations.
  • Online Research: Used to gather scientific information and support the content of the website.
  • ChatGPT: Used for frompt creation and coding error troubleshooting.

✨ Creative Elements

  • 🌎 Real-World Connections: Links actual locations on Earth to possible research opportunities for Moon and Mars exploration.
  • 🔭 Visual Presentation: Combines maps, location details and comparisons to present information clearly.
  • 🎨 User-Friendly Design: Organises complex scientific information into simple, easy-to-navigate sections.
  • 🧠 Self-Guided Learning: Allows users to discover information at their own pace through interactive features.

⚠️ Problems Earth2Space Helps Solve

  • Scattered Research Information: Brings information about potential Earth analog locations together in one accessible platform.
  • Difficulty Identifying Analog Sites: Makes it easier to discover and compare real-world locations that resemble conditions on the Moon and Mars.
  • Limited Public Awareness: Helps people understand why Earth analogs are important for preparing future space missions.
  • Complex Scientific Information: Presents research and environmental data in a simpler, more interactive way.
  • Lack of Interactive Learning: Provides simulations and activities that allow users to experience space exploration challenges rather than just read about them.
  • Mission Preparation Challenges: Helps demonstrate how testing equipment and studying extreme environments on Earth can reduce risks before actual space missions.
